body:
There's something irresistible about a celebrity nursery reveal. The beautiful furniture, perfectly coordinated colors, and little details that make the room feel straight out of a design magazine.

But what if we got to design the nurseries ourselves?

From the warm, welcoming style of Dancing with the Stars' Witney Carson to the sophisticated world of Owning Manhattan's Jessica Markowski, we're imagining how we'd create four different celebrity-inspired nurseries using dadadababy furniture.

These are our own dream designs inspired by their public personalities and stories, not actual nursery reveals or celebrity endorsements. And the best part? You can borrow the same ideas for your own baby's room.

Between Dancing with the Stars and preparing to welcome her third child, Witney Carson has plenty going on. But when it comes to nursery inspiration, we're looking back at the beautiful space she shared for her first son in 2020.

Her nursery featured warm neutrals, earthy textures, an olive-green crib, and meaningful family artwork. It was sophisticated without feeling overly formal, and the personal touches made it especially memorable.

If we were styling a nursery inspired by Witney, we'd start with the dadadababy Soho 3-in-1 Convertible Crib in a natural wood finish. Its clean, mid-century-inspired silhouette would be a beautiful centerpiece against warm ivory walls.

We'd add a muted olive accent, a woven rug, textured curtains, and a comfortable chair. A few carefully chosen family photographs or meaningful illustrations would give the room personality without making it feel cluttered.

And since the Soho crib can convert into a toddler bed and daybed with the appropriate components, we'd be choosing furniture that can stay with the family beyond the newborn stage.

The idea worth stealing: A neutral nursery doesn't need to be plain. Sometimes one unexpected color and a few meaningful details make the biggest difference.

2. Leah Van Dale: Playful, Modern, and Made for Real Family Life

Former WWE star Leah Van Dale, also known as Carmella, has embraced motherhood with her two young sons. And anyone who's spent time around toddlers knows that a nursery needs to be more than beautiful. It needs to work.

For a family with little ones growing up close together, we'd want furniture that's durable, practical, and playful enough to feel right at home in a child's space.

Our pick would be the Jolly 3-in-1 Convertible Crib in White + Natural.

The Jolly's rounded silhouette feels playful without being overly decorative. The mix of white and natural wood adds warmth, while its simple design makes it easy to pair with different colors as a child's room evolves.

We'd style it with a soft cream rug, light wood storage, playful wall prints, and a few warm accent colors. Nothing too precious or difficult to maintain.

A practical dresser with enough space for diapers, clothing, and everyday essentials would complete the room. And we'd make sure there was plenty of open floor space for play.

The idea worth stealing: Choose furniture that's as practical as it is beautiful. A nursery should be able to handle real family life, not just look good in photographs.

3. Jessica Markowski: A City-Chic Nursery With Timeless Appeal

For a completely different aesthetic, we're taking inspiration from Jessica Markowski, known for Netflix's Owning Manhattan and her work in luxury real estate.

Her world of beautiful New York properties makes us think of a nursery that feels like a natural extension of a sophisticated apartment: clean lines, rich materials, and a few carefully selected statement pieces.

We're not drawing from a public nursery reveal here. This is simply the room we'd imagine designing with a polished, city-inspired aesthetic in mind.

We'd start with the Bliss 4-in-1 Convertible Crib in Walnut.

Its rich wood finish and clean lines would look beautiful against cream walls, with a soft textured rug and a few darker accents to create contrast.

Instead of filling every corner, we'd let the furniture speak for itself. A matching or complementary dresser, elegant lighting placed safely away from the crib, and simple framed artwork would give the space a polished look.

For a smaller apartment nursery, we'd also consider a dresser with a compatible removable changing tray instead of a separate changing table. Once diaper changes are behind you, the dresser can continue serving as everyday storage.

The idea worth stealing: Luxury doesn't have to mean more furniture. A few beautiful, functional pieces can make even a compact nursery feel thoughtfully designed.

4. Alexandra Madison: Soft Colors and Meaningful Little Details

Content creator Alexandra Madison and her husband, Jon Bouffard, welcomed their daughter, Lucy Grey, in 2025. Their journey into parenthood has been deeply personal, and Alexandra has spoken publicly about keeping parts of her daughter's life private.

That makes us think about a different kind of nursery design: one that doesn't need to impress anyone online. A room filled with things that mean something to the people who live there.

If we were designing a nursery with that feeling in mind, we'd choose the LaLa 3-in-1 Convertible Crib in Almond Milk or Natural.

Its classic slatted design would work beautifully with soft cream, muted green, and delicate blush accents. We'd add warm lighting, an inviting chair, and a few pieces of artwork chosen for their personal meaning rather than their popularity on Pinterest.

A framed family photograph, a treasured childhood illustration, or a handmade keepsake could make the room feel truly special.

We'd also choose a dresser with timeless lines, something that could hold baby clothes today and still feel right in the room years later.

The idea worth stealing: Your baby's room doesn't need a perfect theme. The little details that tell your family's story will always feel more personal than a trend.

What These Four Nursery Looks Have in Common

From Witney's warm neutrals to the city-inspired design we'd create for Jessica, each of these imaginary spaces has a different personality. But there's one thing we'd prioritize in every room: furniture that feels beautiful today and still works as the child grows.

We'd start with a dadadababy crib as the anchor, then build the room around its finish, silhouette, and dimensions. Solid European beechwood, versatile colors, and simple shapes make it easier to introduce different styles without needing to replace the furniture every time your taste changes.

Rather than trying to match every piece perfectly, we'd combine complementary materials, repeat a few accent colors, and leave room for the family's personality to develop.

Build Warmth Around the Crib, Not Inside It

One detail that's easy to miss in celebrity nursery photographs is the difference between styling a beautiful room and creating a safe sleep space.

We love textured rugs, soft curtains, woven storage, and comfortable chairs. These can make a nursery feel warm and inviting without adding unnecessary decoration inside the crib.

For infant sleep, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends a firm, flat mattress with a properly fitted sheet and no loose blankets, pillows, bumpers, or stuffed toys in the sleep space.

A beautifully styled nursery photo can inspire your color palette, but it shouldn't determine how you prepare your baby's crib for sleep.

Let the Layout Pass the Nighttime Test

Even the most gorgeous nursery needs to work at 2 a.m.

Picture walking into the room with your baby and only a soft light on. Can you get to the crib comfortably? Are diapers and spare clothes easy to reach? Can the dresser drawers open without blocking your path?

Before putting the finishing touches on your celebrity-inspired space, check a few practical details:

  • Crib placement: Keep the crib away from window-covering cords and other reachable cords. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission warns that window cords can pose a strangulation hazard.
  • Lighting: Choose soft nighttime lighting and keep lamps and electrical cords safely away from the crib.
  • Storage: Organize diapers, wipes, and spare clothing in accessible drawers or baskets, but keep them out of your baby's reach.
  • Furniture safety: Anchor dressers according to their instructions, and secure decorative items away from the sleep space.

A few thoughtful layout choices can make a beautiful nursery much easier to live in.

Leave Room for Your Own Story

Here's what we love most about taking inspiration from someone else's home: you can borrow the feeling without copying every detail.

Maybe you love the warm, natural look of Witney Carson's nursery. Maybe you'd rather have something playful and modern, or perhaps your dream nursery looks more like a sophisticated New York apartment.

Whatever your style, remember that the room will change as your baby grows.

Swap artwork, introduce new colors, reorganize storage, and eventually adapt convertible furniture when your child is ready and the manufacturer approves the transition.

A beautiful nursery doesn't have to stay exactly the same forever. In fact, the best rooms are the ones that make space for everything that's still to come.

Questions Parents Ask

How Can I Create a Celebrity-Inspired Nursery on a Budget?

Start with one furniture piece you genuinely love, such as a convertible crib, and build the rest of the room around it. You can create an elevated look with a thoughtful color palette, inexpensive artwork, and practical storage without recreating every detail from a celebrity home.

Do All the Nursery Furniture Pieces Have to Match?

Not at all. Mixing complementary wood finishes, neutral colors, and different textures can make the room feel more personal. Focus on creating a consistent overall palette rather than buying everything from the same collection.

How Do I Keep the Nursery Looking Beautiful as My Child Grows?

Choose furniture that offers long-term usefulness, then change smaller decorative details over time. If you're considering a convertible dadadababy crib, review its specific conversion options and required components so you understand how it can adapt through different stages.

Your Baby Deserves Their Own Beautiful Space

Celebrity nurseries are fun to admire, but you don't need a famous name or an interior designer to create a room you love.

Take a little inspiration from your favorite personalities, choose a few well-made pieces, and add the details that make the space feel like home.

At dadadababy, we believe the most beautiful nursery isn't the one that looks perfect in a photograph. It's the one that feels right for your family.
